newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sees Colmar or Toul as DHL hub site.
newsitem.headline: France sees Colmar or Toul as DHL hub site.

text.p: The French government has proposed two sites at Colmar or Toul for DHL Worldwide Express' disputed Rhine Valley hub, a senior French transport ministry official told Reuters.
DHL had planned to establish the hub in Strasbourg but this collapsed this autumn when the project was contested by residents and local authorities.
"We expect DHL to have made its choice by the end of the year," the official said.
He added that the defence ministry -- which is working closely with its transport counterpart -- has identified two military airfield sites for DHL's proposed hub.
The first is at Toul-Rosieres in Lorraine and the other at Colmar-Meyenheim, situated respectively around 70 miles west and 35 miles south of Strasbourg, the official said.
The Toul-Rosieres airbase is due to close in summer 1998 as part of the country's armed forces rationalisation programme, but military operations are due to continue at the Colmar fighter airbase.

"Defence Minister Charles Millon has a preference for the Toul site but no obstacle would be put in DHL's way if they decided on Colmar which they do appear to favour as it is only three hours by road from Stuttgart, a key factor," he said.
Both sites would require upgrading work entailing either the lengthening or consolidation of the runway before DHL could begin operations, the official said.

"While Toul and Colmar might be termed feasible sites, we do not want to give the impression they are the only ones in the running. There are two other French sites and two German sites under discussion and what is more, we are still open to suggestions on additional ones," DHL Aviation business development manager Steven Lewis told Reuters.

In an earlier statement, Lewis said Toul-Rosieres did not appear to be any better-placed than Metz-Nancy Lorraine airport, a site which DHL had been invited to consider by public authorities in the region but which Lewis described as being too far west from the Franco-German border to be an ideal location.
DHL could not make a decision on the location of the hub until it had received a definitive list of approved sites from the French authorities, Lewis added.
"Clearly we'd like to have a Rhine Valley hub in place as soon as possible. However, at the same time we don't want to rush a project which represents a long-term investment."
Lewis said once the location of the hub was decided, its development would proceed at a slower rate than that envisaged for Strasbourg.

"While establishing a Rhine Valley hub remains a priority, our existing network continues to demonstrate how capable it is of absorbing traffic which had been earmarked for the Strasbourg hub -- even during a period of peak demand such as we have at present."
